source.title: Understanding On-Policy Distillation: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective via Sparse Crosscoders
source.authors: Zi-Chao Yu; Qian-Shuo Ye; Xu Wang; Di-Fan Zou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. There are minor text-extraction artifacts in equations and symbols.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse crosscoders to LLM checkpoints in OPD and teacher-rollout warm-up settings, and reports reconstruction and feature-level intervention results. It does not test toy-model superposition or its geometric predictions.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports sparse crosscoder feature recovery and analyses feature usage, so these results bear on V4. It does not measure feature sparsity relative to model dimensions, near-orthogonality, overlapping directions, neuron polysemanticity, or whether dictionary features are complete, stable canonical units. Rows about OPD accuracy alone and cited findings from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study uses sparse crosscoders (an SAE-style dictionary) as its tool for analysing on-policy distillation. Its claim-adjacent numbers are the tool's own reconstruction quality (FVE about 0.76–0.82) and OPD-specific feature-usage changes. It reports no test of whether LLM features are superposed or spread across neurons, and no test of whether dictionary recovery is evidence for that. Reconstruction quality of the authors' own dictionary is method performance, not a test of V4. The feature-stability and intervention results concern what OPD and SFT warm-up change, not superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that OPD, and the SFT warm-up on teacher rollouts, create no new features and pass on none of the teacher's. Both only reweight features the student shares with the teacher, with OPD's largest changes at decision tokens. Imposing the warm-up's feature reweighting on a directly distilled student (without weight changes) brings its accuracy close to the warmed-up student's, while shuffled features do not.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse crosscoders and a swap readout to analyze LLM feature usage and interventions; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method or test its geometric predictions.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature results vary by teacher setting: the share of frequently used features changing by less than 20% is 98.2% for JustRL, 99.6% for Skywork, and 99.4% for R1-7B. Decision-token feature changes are reported under JustRL and Skywork, but none of the 50 most-changed features fires on a decision token under R1-7B.
record.problems: The claim-relevant LLM evidence is limited to the particular model families, layers, data, and crosscoder setup studied. The paper does not test superposition geometry, compare feature dictionaries against a ground-truth feature set, or establish feature completeness or canonicality. Most feature statistics have no reported uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted for the 60-row cap. OPD benchmark accuracy results from Tables 2, 6, and 7 were left out because accuracy alone does not measure the claim's feature or geometry constructs.

untested.parts: Toy models, feature-count vs dimension, near-orthogonal overlap, sparsity-dependent transition, geometry: none tested.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity: not tested.
Non-capacity origins of polysemanticity: not tested.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no test of whether dictionary recovery reflects superposition. Crosscoder FVE is reported only as tool validation.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of dictionary features across seeds or sizes: not tested. Only a single seed and size (32,768 features) is used.
One-dimensional vs multi-dimensional features: not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3/V4 supports' should be overridden. The paper treats SAE-style crosscoders as an established tool and never asks whether superposition holds. Its reconstruction numbers are a held-out FVE of about 0.81 with about 50 active features out of 32,768, using BatchTopK, at the block-14 residual stream. These are the study's own method-validation figures. Per the rules, they are T4 tool performance rather than evidence on V4. Single seed and single dictionary size, so nothing bears on V5 stability either.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study recovers and analyzes sparse crosscoder features in LLMs, but does not measure whether features are distributed across many neurons or compare SAE recovery with other feature-recovery methods.
The study does not establish whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B-Base

rows.check: Accuracy effect of the authors' feature-level intervention evaluates their method for the OPD question; it is not a measure of superposition.
